Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, and its subordinate offices observe Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026
articles.full_content:
The Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, along with its attached and subordinate offices and field formations, is fully geared up to participate in the upcoming Special Campaign 6.0, being conducted across Government of India departments from 2 nd to 31 st October 2026. The campaign is being spearheaded by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) to further institutionalise Swachhata (cleanliness) and ensure timely and effective disposal of pending references.
As part of the preparatory phase, which commenced on 17 th September 2026, all organizations under the Department of Revenue – including the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Enforcement Directorate, Financial Intelligence Unit – India, and others – have undertaken thorough reviews to identify Pending MP/State Government references, Public grievances, Cleanliness campaigns in offices and public-facing areas, Records for digitization & weeding out and Disposal of scrap, e-waste and obsolete items. Each organisation has designated nodal officers to ensure focused action during the implementation phase. Efforts are underway to sensitise staff and ensure enthusiastic participation at all levels. The Department is also emphasising the use of technology to reduce physical records, promote paperless work environments, and enhance citizen-centric service delivery.
The Department of Revenue had actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0, significantly contributing to the reduction of pendency and promoting a culture of cleanliness. During the period from December 2025 to August, 2026, the Department of Revenue disposed of a total of 65 Inter-Ministerial Reference (Cabinet Notes, CoS Note, EFC Memo etc.), more than 100 VIP references, 12611 Public Grievances, 274 Public Grievances Appeal.
Furthermore, with the scrap disposal, revenue of Rs. 5,03,500/- was also generated.
Special Campaign 6.0 reaffirms the Department of Revenue's commitment to overall cleanliness, e-waste disposal, space management, transparency, and accountability to further enhance administrative efficiency and cleanliness across all levels.

Release of Draft Guideline for Compilation Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates by Expenditure Approach with Base Year 2022-23
articles.full_content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, has prepared the draft guideline for Compilation of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates from Expenditure Side with Base Year 2022-23. The guideline is being released and uploaded on the official website of MoSPI (link attached below).
The draft guideline provides a uniform and comprehensive framework for compilation of GSDP estimates from the expenditure side across States and Union Territories, with the objective of ensuring consistency, comparability and methodological standardization under the revised base year framework.
The draft guideline elaborates the concepts, coverage, data sources, estimation procedures and methodologies for compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side, covering the major expenditure components, including Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE), Government Final Consumption Expenditure (GFCE), Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF), Changes in Inventories, Valuables and Net Exports. At present, some States/UTs are compiling estimates of GFCF and GFCE; however, PFCE estimates are not being compiled by any State/UT. The document, therefore, provides a comprehensive framework and methodological guidance to facilitate the compilation of these expenditure components at the State/UT level.
The guideline emphasizes the use of State-specific data sources and appropriate allocation indicators for estimation of various expenditure components, to the extent feasible. In cases where direct State-level data are not available, suitable allocation methodologies and relevant indicators have been recommended for deriving State-wise estimates in a consistent and comparable manner.
The compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side provides an important complementary approach to the production/income-side estimation of GSDP and would facilitate a comprehensive assessment of economic activity at the State/UT level. The estimates would also contribute towards strengthening the State-level national accounts framework and improving the consistency of State estimates with the methodology followed at the national level.
The release of draft guideline is an important step towards harmonization of estimation practices across States/UTs and strengthening the statistical capacity of State Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DESs) for the compilation of expenditure-side GSDP estimates.
The draft Guideline is available on the official website of MoSPI ( https://www.mospi.gov.in/product/more/6-Documents ) for wider dissemination and feedback from stakeholders by 28 th October, 2026

The guideline is being released and uploaded on the official website of MoSPI (link attached below). The draft guideline provides a uniform and comprehensive framework for compilation of GSDP estimates from the expenditure side across States and Union Territories, with the objective of ensuring consistency, comparability and methodological standardization under the revised base year framework.

Implementation of Swachhta Hi Seva Campaign 2026 in NITI Aayog from 17th September, 2026 to 2nd October, 2026
articles.full_content:
As a run up to Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 nd October, 2026, a day that the nation celebrates the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Dept. of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti organised the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ campaign from 17 th September to 2 nd October, 2026, in collaboration with other Ministries, to celebrate 12 years of Swachh Bharat Mission, to reaffirm the commitment of all to make India clean and garbage free. The theme for SHS 2026 is “ S wachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat ”.
NITI Aayog actively participated in the campaign during the period, and the major events organised under the Department during the campaign are as follows:
• Inspection of Record Room in NITI Aayog : An Inspection of the Record Room in NITI Aayog was conducted on 24 th September 2026 by the senior officers with special emphasis on file reviewing, weeding out & digitisation of old records and disposal of scrap.
• Awareness Campaign: The campaign banners & standees were installed all across NITI Aayog gates, outdoor areas and office premises for generating awareness amongst Officers/Staff of NITI Aayog. SHS-2026 campaign banners were also displayed on the NITI Aayog Website Homepage for the campaign duration.
• Cleanliness Drive in NITI Aayog Office Premises : A Cleanliness Drive was conducted in NITI Aayog Office Premises on all floors from 24 th September 2026 to 30 th September 2026 with active participation of NITI Aayog staff.
• Deep Cleaning of NITI Aayog Departmental Canteen : The Welfare Team undertook the activity of deep cleaning of NITI Aayog Departmental Canteen Hall & Kitchen from 24 th September 2026 to 30 th September 2026 .
• Swachhta Pledge : Observing the nationwide Shramdaan campaign, “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath,” on 1 st October 2026, the Hon’ble Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, administered the Swachhta Pledge to NITI Aayog staff, followed by a cleanliness drive across the outdoor campus, in the presence of Hon’ble Members, NITI Aayog and officials and staff of NITI Aayog.

articles.full_content:
A One-Day Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme was organized by the MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal , on 09 October 2026 at the Conference Hall, Kakching Municipal Council (KMC), Kakching, Manipur. The programme brought together PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries and key stakeholders to strengthen awareness on branding, marketing, entrepreneurship, financial literacy and digital tools.
The programme was organized as a continuation of the Branding and Marketing awareness initiatives undertaken by MSME-DFO, Imphal, across different districts of Manipur . Similar programmes have already been conducted in Imphal East, Imphal West and Thoubal , collectively reaching more than 500 PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries . The strong participation of 100 beneficiaries attended in Kakching further reflected the growing interest among traditional artisans in strengthening their enterprises through improved branding, marketing and digital adoption.
Shri Elangbam Anand Singh, MCS, ADM, Kakching District , attended the programme as the Chief Guest. In his address, he highlighted the importance of strengthening traditional skills and enterprises and encouraged artisans to adopt appropriate approaches to improve productivity, market opportunities and livelihoods.
Shri M. Siva Sai Reddy, IEDS, Assistant Director, Ministry of MSME , delivered the welcome address and set the context for the programme, highlighting the importance of supporting traditional artisans through awareness, capacity building and institutional support under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.
Shri Oinam Deben Singh, General Manager, District Industries Centre (DIC) , addressed the gathering and highlighted the role of institutional support in facilitating the growth and development of local enterprises and entrepreneurs.
Shri Guneshwor Singh, Lead District Manager (LDM) , conducted a session on Financial Literacy, Credit Linkages and Institutional Support for PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries . The session focused on improving beneficiaries’ understanding of financial services, credit facilities and available institutional support.
The technical sessions focused on strengthening the productivity and market readiness of artisans. Smt. H. Shubra Devi, Founder, Meira Foods , shared practical insights on skill development, market trends and sales strategies , with emphasis on improving productivity and responding to changing market demands.
Shri Jiban Khundrakpam, Branding Consultant, Manipro Branding Solutions , conducted a session on entrepreneurship development, export opportunities, branding, packaging and product design , highlighting the importance of product presentation and branding in accessing wider markets.
Shri Abhishek Kesarwani, YP , MSME-DFO, Imphal , sensitized the beneficiaries on MSME Schemes and Udyam Registration , providing information on formalization and the institutional support available to micro and small enterprises.

Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches World Bank Group’s ‘World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence’ in New Delhi
articles.full_content:
Report sets out a framework for developing economies to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement IndiaAI Mission, MeitY and the World Bank Group jointly host the India launch; policymakers, development experts and technology leaders deliberate on scaling AI for inclusive development High-level panel and State AI Showcase examine how India can move from isolated AI pilots to evidence-based scale-up across sectors
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways, and Information and Broadcasting, today launched the World Bank Group’s World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence at an event held at The Oberoi, New Delhi. The Report examines the opportunities and challenges that Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents for developing economies, and sets out a framework for countries to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement.
The launch was organised by the IndiaAI Mission, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the World Bank Group. It brought together senior policymakers, global development experts, technology leaders and practitioners to deliberate on how India can maximise, and safely sustain, the development gains from AI. The programme also featured a State AI Showcase, in which States and innovators presented AI-enabled solutions from across the country.
The Report notes that AI can widen access to expertise, raise productivity and improve the delivery of services in developing economies. AI-enabled tools are already being deployed in medical screening, agricultural decision-making and education, extending scarce expertise to larger sections of the population. The Report further emphasises that these gains rest on strong foundations, including reliable electricity and connectivity, computing infrastructure, quality data, skills, education systems and capable institutions.
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister of Electronics and IT delivered the keynote address and formally presented the Report. The Union Minister underlined India’s approach of democratising technology, so that the benefits of Artificial Intelligence reach citizens, enterprises and institutions across the country.
“AI is changing the lives of ordinary people. In Baramati, sugarcane yields rose by 40 per cent with 30 per cent less water and fertiliser, for farmers who have never used a computer simply through voice on a phone. In healthcare, TB detection has increased by 35 per cent. Examples like these can change lives across the Global South and the world,” said Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw.
The Union Minister added that the Baramati initiative draws on satellite, IoT and weather data and has also lowered labour costs. In Gujarat, AgriStack is being used by 5 lakh farmers, and AI for animal health through Sarlaben is benefiting 3 crore cattle and their farmers.

Department of Biotechnology launches Special Campaign 6 with focus on E-waste Management and impactful initiatives reaffirming its commitment to promote cleanliness, hygiene and a culture of responsible workplace practices
articles.full_content:
Department of Biotechnology, under the aegis of Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DAR&PG) has accelerated efforts for achieving 100% targets in reducing pendency, Record management and coverage of all Campaign sites. The Department, in collaboration with Scientific Cadre Units, Divisions and its Autonomous Institutions & PSUs, is enthusiastically participating in the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 as announced by Govt. of India from 2 nd – 31 st October 2026 for cleanliness and disposal of e-waste material for enhancing work place experience. Progress of the campaign is being regularly reviewed by Secretary and Joint Secretary & Nodal Officer for the campaign.
During the Preparatory Phase (15–30 September 2026) , the Department set key targets, including reviewing and organizing 18,741 e-files, 7,773 physical files , undertaking cleanliness and space-clearing activities at 156 sites to create 46,486 square feet of usable space , disposal of 1,694 e-waste items and generating revenue of ₹ 39,33,055 from disposal of e-waste and non e-waste items.
The Department of Biotechnology observed Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 nd October 2026 by organizing an e-waste disposal drive under Special Campaign 6 reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness and responsible waste management. The programme was led by Secretary (DBT) at the DBT (HQ), CGO Complex, Delhi, and was attended by senior officers of the Department. On the occasion, Secretary, DBT urged everyone to take personal responsibility for maintaining clean surroundings by properly identifying and disposing of obsolete items, e-waste, and unserviceable materials at home and workplace. He emphasized the growing need for responsible management of electronic assets and systematic disposal of obsolete records / scrap material to create both financial value for the public exchequer and usable space for Government offices.
The Department also conducted a Special cleanliness drive “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” under chairpersonship of Ms Ekta Vishnoi, Joint Secretary (Admn) on 1 October, 2026 with the participation of all officers/staff in a one-hour mass cleanliness drive/shramdaan from 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM in public park near JLN Metro Station followed by Plantation of saplings under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative.
As part of activities under Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign- 2026, the Department also organized Kabbad Se Kala – Waste to Art under the theme of Swachhata Se Samridhi in which participants has given discarded materials a second life through creative Waste to Art. These displays carry a simple message: with a little imagination, nothing is truly waste. Let's institutionalize Swachhata, clear pendency, and make Reduce, Reuse, Recycle a daily habit at every desk.

articles.title: MoSPI signs MoU with Pahle India Foundation, New Delhi to strengthen collaboration in Official Statistics, Research and Data Analysis
articles.full_content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Pahle India Foundation (PIF), New Delhi to strengthen collaboration in the areas of official statistics, research, data analysis, capacity building and knowledge sharing.
The signing ceremony was graced by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General, MoSPI, and Dr. Rajiv Kumar, Chairperson, PIF, Shri Ashish Kumar, Chief Statistician, PIF. The MoU was signed by Ms. Sunitha Bhaskar, Additional Director General, MoSPI, and Mr. Ravi Pokharna, Executive Director, Pahle India Foundation. The occasion was also attended by senior officers/ officials of MoSPI and representatives from the Pahle India Foundation.
The MoU aims to provide a broad framework for collaboration between MoSPI and Pahle India Foundation, New Delhi in areas of mutual interest, including research, data analysis, capacity building and knowledge sharing, with specific collaborative activities to be undertaken based on the priorities of MoSPI.

Department of Economic Affairs observes Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026
articles.full_content:
The Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance, along with its attached/subordinate offices and organisations under its administrative control, is undertaking Special Campaign 6.0 from 2 nd to 31 st October, 2026. The Campaign is being implemented across Government under the coordination of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata , reducing pendency, improving record management and enhancing the experience of citizens in Government offices.
A key focus of Special Campaign 6.0 is “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” , building upon the emphasis on scientific management of e-waste in previous campaigns. The Campaign seeks to ensure responsible handling and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, while also promoting cleanliness, efficient use of office space and improved workplace experience. Particular attention is being given to field and outstation offices providing public services or having direct public interface.
During the Campaign, DEA is undertaking focused action on the identification and disposal of pending references from Members of Parliament, State Governments, inter-Ministerial references, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, Public Grievances and grievance appeals. The Campaign also provides an opportunity to strengthen record management through review, categorisation, recording and weeding out of physical records and closure of e-files, in accordance with extant Government guidelines.
As part of the Campaign, DEA is also undertaking cleanliness drives, space management, disposal of scrap and redundant materials, and identification and implementation of process simplification measures. The Department is coordinating with its concerned offices and organisations for effective implementation and monitoring of the identified targets. The Campaign also encourages adoption and documentation of best practices, including initiatives relating to e-waste management, digitization, efficient management of space, environment-friendly practices, citizen-centric initiatives and innovative practices.
The implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 is being monitored through the SCDPM portal, with progress being reviewed on a regular basis. DEA remains committed to achieving tangible outcomes through the Campaign and to sustaining the gains achieved in Swachhata , e-waste management, pendency reduction, record management, efficient use of office space and citizen-centric service delivery.

Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Organises World Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day 2026
articles.full_content:
Government, Industry and Experts Come Together to Discuss the Safe Use of Hydrogen
On the occasion of World Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) organised an event at the Atal Akshay Urja Bhawan, New Delhi. Over 100 government officials, industry representatives, researchers and experts took part in discussions on the standards and safety measures needed for the use of Hydrogen in India.
The event included two panel discussions on Hydrogen standards and safety at Hydrogen facilities. Representatives from the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD), and other research and industry organisations joined the discussions.
Participants shared their experiences and discussed how clear standards and safety measures can support the wider use of Hydrogen in India.
The discussions emphasised the need to establish clear standards for producing, storing, transporting and using Hydrogen, better testing and training to help people work safely with Hydrogen, and closer coordination between government agencies, industry and experts.
The valedictory session was graced by Chief guest Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. Shri Akash Tripathi, Managing Director, Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI), delivered the special address, while Shri Mohammad Rihan, Director General, National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), also addressed the gathering. Shri Abhay Bakre, Mission Director, National Green Hydrogen Mission, MNRE, gave the opening remarks. Shri Sujit Pillai, Scientist F, MNRE, delivered the vote of thanks.
A report titled “India’s Hydrogen Standards: Gap Assessment and Preliminary Action Framework”, prepared in association with Boston Consulting Group (BCG), was also released at the event. The report analyses the existing Hydrogen standards, identified in the country and areas that need attention and steps to address them.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved in January 2023 with an outlay of ₹19,744 crore. It aims to make India a global hub for producing, using and exporting green Hydrogen and related products. The Mission targets an annual green Hydrogen production capacity of 5 million metric tonnes by 2030. It supports production, equipment manufacturing, pilot projects, research and training.

Over 100 government officials, industry representatives, researchers and experts took part in discussions on the standards and safety measures needed for the use of Hydrogen in India. The event included two panel discussions on Hydrogen standards and safety at Hydrogen facilities.
